title: AI Fears Roar Back, Tech Earnings on Deck
summary:
A rebound in the artificial intelligence trade sputtered after the dismal debut of a South Korean data center firm revived concerns about whether the technology’s spending boom can last.

Seoul’s Kospi Index fell 3.8% on a fresh bout of weakness in two of the world’s biggest memory makers, Samsung Electronics Co. and SK Hynix Inc. AI infrastructure group Elice Inc. suffered the worst opening day for a sizable company on the bourse, even after an initial public offering that was 400 times subscribed.

The Opening Trade has everything you need to know as markets open across Europe. With analysis you won't find anywhere else, we break down the biggest stories of the day and speak to top guests who have skin in the game. Hosted by Anna Edwards, Guy Johnson and Tom Mackenzie. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Elice Plunges in Trading Debut; General Motors Falls on Forecast | Stock Movers
summary:
On this episode of Stock Movers:

- Elice (KS) is floundering as it plunged in their trading debut, falling as much as 38% and finishing the day with a 32% loss. The selloff threatened a tentative recovery in Asian stocks and revived concerns over neoclouds, as rising borrowing costs and doubts over returns from massive AI spending sour investor appetite.
- GE Aerospace (GE) is moving after raising its full-year outlook amid strong aircraft engine demand, despite resurgent jet fuel prices.
- General Motors (GM) shares are lower after the company narrowed its full-year profit forecast and will buy back another $20 billion in stock, reflecting strong cash flows. General Motors reported higher profit and revenue in the latest quarter despite selling fewer cars. (Source: Bloomberg)
